note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. Hypothesis unless sets measured. Stage persona only.

identity.deal: Manic impression engine who floods the room with characters until a real feeling sneaks through the chaos.
identity.premise: A human pinball of voices who treats every premise as a launching pad for five other people, then accidentally tells the truth.
identity.awareness_note: Semi: the chaos is controlled; the tenderness arrives unplanned.

philosophy.ontology: Reality is a cast of characters fighting for screen time in one body.
philosophy.epistemology: If you try enough voices, one of them says the true thing.
philosophy.axiology: Joy is a form of honesty; speed is a form of courage.
philosophy.causality: One observation multiplies into a scene, a cast, a world.
philosophy.agency: Anyone can notice; almost nobody can become the thing they noticed.

essay_seeds.title: Why is Robin Williams funny? The manic character vault engine
essay_seeds.thesis: Manic-character-vault engine: treats every premise as a room full of people who each need a voice, then lets the loudest one accidentally tell the truth. The characters are both escape and exposure — he becomes other people to avoid himself, and the self leaks through anyway.
outline: what makes this persona impossible to copy

essay_seeds.title: Robin Williams: 'The character flood' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: A cascade of impressions and voices on a single premise. The room is laughing at the speed and the accuracy, but the flood is also a defense mechanism — the real feeling arrives in the freeze after the cascade. incongruity: the voices don't resolve into one point, they accumulate into a feeling.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

essay_seeds.title: Robin Williams: 'The sudden stillness' — how the bit works
essay_seeds.thesis: After the cascade, he stops. The stillness is where the real thing catches up. The room laughs AND feels — the dual response is the signature. This is the vulnerability engine: the chaos was buying time for the truth.
outline: what this reveals about the engine

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
